Hi Sophie — thanks, we can kick this off. Attaching Redwood's current editable DPA template plus our published subprocessor inventory. Quick notes up front: 

- Attachment: Redwood_DPA_Template_v2.docx (editable)
- Attachment: Redwood_Subprocessor_List.xlsx (current as of 2025-10-01)

eSign: Redwood supports both DocuSign and AdobeSign. For automated routing and tracking we currently default to DocuSign, but we can accept an AdobeSign-signed DPA if Novacorp must use it. Please confirm preference and whether you require signer order / witness rules.

2) Novacorp legal: mark up the attached DPA and return with redlines.
3) Redwood legal (cc'd Karthik): we'll review and propose comments in 3 business days after receipt.

Looping Laura for procurement coordination on quoting/credits questions.

Subject: Novacorp proposed redlines (DPA)

Irene — attaching our redlines and a short cover note. High level items we changed: 

- Data transfer clause: we prefer an explicit UK Addendum reference and additional audit rights for transfers to non-EEA subprocessors.
- Subprocessor approval: we've requested a right to object within 15 days for new subprocessors handling payment or identity data.
- Liability & caps: proposed carveouts for breach-related audit costs.

Attachment: Novacorp_Redlines_v1.pdf (generated from Word comments)

We can accept DocuSign for execution; however, for the initial signatory sequence we need a two-step execution (Novacorp Countersign after Redwood signs). Also please confirm whether Redwood can commit to providing subprocessor notices 30 days before onboarding.

Thanks,
Novacorp Legal

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 03 Nov 2025 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Novacorp proposed redlines (DPA) — internal alignment and exec path

Irene/Laura — quick internal note before we reply to Novacorp: 

- Legal: we should accept the UK Addendum reference; it's standard and low risk.
- Subprocessor objection window: 15 days is short but not unreasonable; recommend proposing 30 days for operational buffer, with a materiality carve (only for subprocessors handling regulated PII or payments).
- eSign routing: DocuSign is easiest operationally. I suggest we prepare a DocuSign room with the editable DPA and a two-step signer flow (Redwood sign -> Novacorp countersign). If Novacorp insists on AdobeSign, we can convert prior to upload but note it tends to break field mapping in our templates.

Action items: 
- Irene: respond to Novacorp confirming DocuSign preference, outline proposed change to the objection window (30 days with materiality carve), and agree on SCCs + UK Addendum.
- Laura: prepare procurement note on quoting hold until DPA is executed; flag any credits if negotiation extends over 14 days.

I'll draft the reply and attach a DocuSign room link stub for internal review.

Karthik
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference
